governing_text: An Extraction, the analysis of one paragraph under passages/FORMAT.md, is the source of every paragraph Move, and it is written by a fixed row on the shared supervisor with a run record rather than by a session, so that a wrong Move can be traced to the Extraction or to the ingest and the stage can be run again on the same input. [implemented-against: passages/FORMAT.md "The paragraph unit", copied 2026-10-15]

Extraction seems particularly important, so we should establish a fixed Prompt for it." The row belongs to the Proof Sheet and changes no production executable; whether a production Extractor adopts it is a separate decision.

judge.note: Every unit is a headless session, a `claude -p` child that runs with no tools (`--tools ""`), spawned by the shared Detached Job supervisor (src/workflow/detached-job.mjs). The model and both bounds NAME THE BRIEF'S SETTINGS, because the Issue gives this row the same bounds as the Brief's. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` replaces the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY.

job.note: ONE JOB PER PARAGRAPH, ONE UNIT PER JOB, run in the Leg's order: paragraph N's input carries the reader state paragraph N-1's Extraction left, so N cannot start before N-1 is written. A call past `brief.call_limit_s` is stopped and spends one attempt, a refused answer spends one, an unreadable answer is asked again without spending one, and a paragraph that has spent `brief.unit_attempts` stops the run naming the paragraph and its last refusal; the Extractions already written stay.

extraction_unit.note: The one call per paragraph (kogaki#1384). `src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs` renders this row through the shared `judgePrompt` renderer, FORMAT.md verbatim above the input marker, and the paragraph's own input below it; `validateExtractionUnit` reads the answer back against FORMAT and `extractionFileText` writes it in FORMAT's layout, so `tools/move_ingest.py passage --from-extraction` reads it unchanged. The header lines the Harness can count or knows -- `unit:`, `length:`, `functions:`, the status line -- and each Segment's quoted opening words are written by the Harness, never asked.
extraction_unit.judgment_point: write the Extraction of ONE paragraph -- `paragraph_you_must_extract` in the input -- under passages/FORMAT.md, rendered above, as a PARAGRAPH-UNIT Extraction: "The paragraph unit"'s six rules govern, and they override the protocol's human round -- there is no step 2, no candidate is written, and you answer Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 yourself, one answer each. Read `earlier_paragraphs` first (rule 2): the reader you describe has just read them. Section 2: write all five reader dimensions in FORMAT's order; where `reader_state_before` is given, every row's `before` is that state copied EXACTLY, character for character (rule 3); where it is null this is the Leg's first paragraph and `before` is the state of the reader `persona` describes. `after` is the literal `unchanged` where this paragraph does not move the row, otherwise the new state in one short clause, and `segment` names the Segment number(s) after which the new state holds (rule 6). At least one row changes. Section 3: ONE SEGMENT PER SENTENCE, in the order of `sentences` -- the Harness has cut them, and your Segment N is sentence N. Each carries its function (raises | advances | settles), its relation to the Segment before it (cause | consequence | contrast | elaboration | evidence | enumeration | none), `content` -- what it does to the reader, written about this paragraph's own content -- and `generalized` -- the same thing stated subject-free, the way section 6 is written, naming no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of your `subject_nouns`, so that it could be performed on any subject. Segment 1's relation is its relation to the previous paragraph's last point and is not `none` (rule 5) unless `earlier_paragraphs` is empty. Sections 4 to 7 as FORMAT writes them; section 6, `technique`, names none of your `subject_nouns`; section 7, `name`, is a snake_case verb phrase naming the transformation, not the topic, and is none of `names_taken`. Section 8, `notes`, may be empty and never carries a `split:` line: the paragraph's boundary is the source's own. Write everything in English except where you quote the paragraph.
extraction_unit.input_shape: ONE Extraction record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT, with exactly these keys: `version` "1"; `paragraph` -- the number of the paragraph in the input; `source`, `prior_text` and `language` -- FORMAT's header lines, one line each; `subject_nouns` -- an array of strings, empty for none; `answers` -- `{ "q1": <one sentence>, "q2": <one sentence>, "q3": <one sentence>, "q4": <one sentence> }`; `what_it_does` -- section 1, one sentence; `reader` -- section 2, exactly five entries in the order knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust, each `{ "dimension": <its name>, "before": <state>, "after": "unchanged" | <new state>, "segment": <"" where after is unchanged, otherwise Segment number(s) such as "2" or "2, 3"> }`; `segments` -- section 3, one entry per sentence in order, each `{ "function": <raises|advances|settles>, "relation": <cause|consequence|contrast|elaboration|evidence|enumeration|none>, "content": <one clause>, "generalized": <one clause> }`; `why_this_order` -- section 3's closing sentence; `presupposes` -- section 4, two or three lines as one string; `breaks` -- section 5, `{ "remove": <line>, "reorder": <line>, "extend": <line> }`; `technique` -- section 6, two or three sentences; `name` -- section 7; `notes` -- section 8, a string, empty for nothing. Every string is one line: no line breaks and no `|`.
extraction_unit.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; `version` not "1"; `paragraph` naming another paragraph; an empty answer or section; `reader` not the five dimensions in FORMAT's order; a `before` that differs from `reader_state_before` where one was given; a changed row naming no Segment, or a Segment number the paragraph does not have; no row changed; `segments` not one entry per sentence; a function or relation outside its set; a Segment missing its `content` or its `generalized` clause; Segment 1's relation `none` where earlier paragraphs exist; a `subject_nouns` entry appearing in a `generalized` clause or in `technique`; a `name` not in the library's id form (lower-case letters, digits and underscores) or already in `names_taken`; a `split:` line in `notes`; a line break or a `|` in any string. Each refusal names the field, and is put back into your next attempt verbatim.
